source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It is within the expected adult temperature range and requires no assessment for illness unless the client also develops hypotension.","B":"It indicates hypothermia and should prompt warming measures before evaluating infectious, inflammatory, or other possible causes.","C":"It is only a mildly elevated temperature below the usual fever threshold, so no additional assessment is needed unless it rises further.","D":"It represents fever and warrants assessment for the underlying cause, associated symptoms, hydration, and other clinical findings."}}
source_row.rationale: An oral temperature of 39.2°C (102.6°F) is clearly febrile. Option D is correct because the nurse should recognize fever and assess the surrounding clinical context and possible cause. Option A incorrectly places the value within the expected adult range. Option B reverses the interpretation by calling a high temperature hypothermia. Option C incorrectly describes 39.2°C as below the fever threshold and advises no additional assessment.
